item.title: AI researchers debate how close we are to recursive self-improvement (Dwarkesh Podcast)
item.description:
Dwarkesh Patel with John Schulman, Beren Millidge, and Charlie O’Neill on how close frontier labs are to AI systems that can improve themselves — and what that would change.
Watch: https://youtu.be/PrSf7IOYu-I
Episode: https://www.dwarkesh.com/p/john-beren-charlie

item.title: 709. The Terror: The Execution of Marie Antoinette (Part 3) (The Rest Is History)
item.description:
Tom Holland and Dominic Sandbrook on Marie Antoinette’s year in prison after Louis XVI’s execution, the factions that argued over her fate, and how she met the guillotine on 16 October 1793.
Episode: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/the-terror-the-execution-of-marie-antoinette-part-3/id1537788786?i=1000789800237
item.itunes:author: The Rest Is History

item.title: Mark Normand: How to Make Your Writing More Funny (How I Write)
item.description:
Mark Normand on how he learned to write comedy after arriving in New York as a nobody — joke construction, bombing, and getting funny on the page.
Watch: https://youtu.be/oXxwMLPZOZE
Episode: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/mark-normand-how-to-make-your-writing-more-funny-how-i-write/id1700171470?i=1000792026873

item.title: What Humans, Animals and Plants Tell Us About Consciousness | Michael Pollan (Huberman Lab)
item.description:
Andrew Huberman with Michael Pollan on consciousness across humans, animals, and plants — what science can say about subjective experience, and where the hard problem still resists.
Watch: https://youtu.be/nk15CT41MFc
Episode: https://www.hubermanlab.com/episode/what-humans-animals-and-plants-tell-us-about-consciousness-michael-pollan

item.description:
Sean Carroll with philosopher Gregg Caruso on hard incompatibilism: why he rejects free will, what that means for blame and criminal justice, and how to keep love, choice, and responsibility without desert.
Watch: https://youtu.be/mQBnjImNOm0
Episode: https://preposterousuniverse.com/podcast/2026/09/28/369-gregg-caruso-on-living-well-without-free-will/

item.title: Noam Brown – Agent swarms, alignment, & recursive self-improvement (Dwarkesh Podcast)
item.description:
Dwarkesh Patel with OpenAI’s Noam Brown on multi-agent systems, what math progress implies for recursive self-improvement, and how to tell if models are actually aligned before RSI.
Watch: https://youtu.be/6AgOfiZOWiY
Episode: https://www.dwarkesh.com/p/noam-brown

item.title: Michael Arndt: Oscar-Winning Writer Teaches Storytelling (How I Write)
item.description:
David Perell with screenwriter Michael Arndt on Pixar’s story craft, what separates a weak script from a strong one, and how to diagnose structure when a story stalls.
Watch: https://youtu.be/gi3xYwX7PN4
Episode: https://howiwrite.substack.com/p/michael-arndt-oscar-winning-writer

item.title: 898: An Argument (This American Life)
item.description:
This American Life revisits Nikole Hannah-Jones’s argument about choosing a public school for her daughter — and what happens when the child who lived that choice gets to answer back.
Episode: https://www.thisamericanlife.org/898/an-argument
item.itunes:author: This American Life

item.title: Archive: Rosalind Franklin (In Our Time)
item.description:
Melvyn Bragg and guests on Rosalind Franklin — the X-ray crystallography behind the DNA double helix, and how credit for the discovery was divided after her death.

item.itunes:author: In Our Time

item.description:
Tom and Dominic on Robespierre’s Reign of Terror: how revolutionary virtue hardened into emergency rule, denunciation, and the machinery that consumed its own coalition.

item.title: How to Make a Difference: Part 1 (Hidden Brain)

Hidden Brain with Martin Seligman on learned helplessness and explanatory style — how the story you tell about a setback can freeze agency or reopen it.
